questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have wanted to go on exchange since I started university. Scotland was a dream destination, as I had travelled there before and loved the country, therefore it had been my ideal location for an exchange for a long time. The fact that they speak English was also a big plus.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive an information mail prior to the stay which Scottish students get sent, I think it got lost in spam or something, so not the easiest because it was a clinical programme, which meant that there wasn't any official sites og descriptions of the stay as I would expect with a university/study exchange programme. However the team at the hospital was very helpful, when I contacted them.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The administration of the medical students was very helpful, and they just introduced me to people and the hospital.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not easy, I did it through some personal connections

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I didn't know that the hospital actually offers free accommodation, so I would definitely just get that sorted out with the administration.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would have chosen the student accommodation if I knew it beforehand.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very helpfull staff.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Just met up the first day and got introduced + got my access card etc.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The medical student administration, and I also felt comfortable with contacting my supervisors.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I didn't have classes as it was a clinical stay.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They are very keen on helping and explaining, so just ask if needed.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I believe that I have done just as much clinical work in Scotland as I would have in Denmark. They are very used to student having learning objectives that has to be done and signed off, and therefore very used to include students. The level is very similar when you consider it in regards to the learning objectives of the logbook.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Doing clinical work focusing on the learning objectives from the logbook.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
5 weeks Clinical Course in Internal Medicine
5 weeks Clinical Course in Clinical Surgery
2 weeks Clinical Course in Anaesthesia

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The stay was the clinical rotation from University of Copenhagen. Therefore I had a supervisor for each rotation/course, which worked very well.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was more like a work place-experience than a university-experience, so there was no clubs or anything like that.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing at the hospital.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you're at the student accommodation, there might be some social activities planned there.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Glasgow and Edinburgh. Go to the Highlands and Islands.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy because they speak English. Since it is not a university the environment is rather local/not international, and some of the structrural/cultural things in conversations could be a bit more difficult to pick up on. However I think that Scottish people as a whole are very welcoming, open and helpfull, which made the social aspect of being here without other exchange student a very good experience.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Because it is almost only people from Scotland or in the Scottish educational/health care system it can be difficult to pick up everything in bigger conversations.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How friendly and open most of the people are.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Consider your interests in any specialties - they are very keen to plan out a stay where you do and experience the things that you like, and it is very flexible as the stay is supposed to be on "University of Copenhagen-terms" with the rotations, and you have a lot of saying in the planning of these. If you want to go to theaters, a lot of doctors are happy for you to join.
2. They have some weekly teachings for the Scottish university students - join them if you would like a break from the clinical stuff.
3. Get ahead with the logbook from the start - there are a lot to get through.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any information mail prior to the stay which Scottish students get sent, I think it got lost in spam or something, so if you don't receive anything I would advise you to contact the student administration.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The helpfulness and attentiveness of the staff both in a professional and personal manner- everyone is very happy to help you to achieve learning objectives or just find your way to the wards when you get lost in the hospital. My supervisors have been great and very dedicated in planning out my stay, and I have not felt forgotten or anything like that even once.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing my social life at home, as it has been limited here. However I think that staying in student accommodation would have changed that, and maybe you can contact University of Glasgow if you want to join clubs or sports.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
